mechanism_inventory: access-control mismatch — redeemEth/redeemWeth no access control beyond onlyIfWeHaveEnoughReserves
value exceeds bound — onlyIfWeHaveEnoughReserves uses strict > instead of >=, last reserve unit unredeemable
wrong lifecycle ordering — removeLiquidityEth burns dcntEth then withdraws WETH; if transfer fails dcntEth already destroyed
external-call failure / DoS — payable(msg.sender).transfer(amount) reverts if msg.sender rejects ETH
stale accounting snapshot — redeemEth/redeemWeth do NOT check/decrement balanceOf, enabling double-withdrawal via removeLiquidityEth afterward
missing invariant enforcement — no check dcntEth supply == weth reserves

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: redeemEth and redeemWeth do not check or decrement balanceOf[msg.sender]. A liquidity provider who deposited via addLiquidityEth (which increments balanceOf) can redeem via redeemEth (burning dcntEth) while their balanceOf credit remains intact, then call removeLiquidityEth (which checks/decrements balanceOf) to withdraw the same ETH a second time — double-spend of their liquidity position.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any user who added liquidity via addLiquidityEth. No privileged role; permissionless after deposit.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. addLiquidityEth{value:X} -> balanceOf[attacker]+=X, WETH deposited, dcntEth minted to address(this). 2. Attacker obtains dcntEth (e.g. via cross-chain receive). 3. redeemEth(X) -> dcntEth.transferFrom(attacker,router,X), weth.withdraw(X), transfer X ETH to attacker; balanceOf unchanged. 4. removeLiquidityEth(X) -> checks balanceOf>=X (still X), burns dcntEth from router, weth.withdraw(X), transfer X ETH again. Result: 2X ETH for X deposited.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol liquidity pool / other LPs — reserve drained 2X for one X contribution.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker gains X ETH free (double withdrawal).
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Direct fund-loss path; balanceOf never decremented in redeemEth/redeemWeth; distinct from the reserves-check mechanism; permissionless after initial deposit.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: onlyIfWeHaveEnoughReserves uses strict > (weth.balanceOf(this) > amount) rather than >=. When the contract holds exactly amount WETH, the check fails even though it could satisfy the redemption — last unit of reserves can never be redeemed, locking it until more liquidity is added.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any redemption caller when reserves equal exactly the requested amount; systematic griefing of the last LP.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. reserve == amount. 2. redeemEth(amount). 3. check weth.balanceOf > amount -> false. 4. revert. 5. remaining WETH unwithdrawable until new deposits.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: LPs trying to withdraw the final unit; WETH stuck.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Clears Medium (stuck funds / availability); different state variable (reserve threshold) than the double-withdrawal mechanism.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In removeLiquidityEth, dcntEth.burn(address(this), amount) executes before weth.withdraw and payable(msg.sender).transfer; wrong lifecycle ordering with an external transfer that can fail.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any LP that is a contract wallet rejecting ETH, or any weth.withdraw failure.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Contract wallet calls removeLiquidityEth(amount). 2. dcntEth.burn. 3. weth.withdraw. 4. transfer reverts -> whole tx reverts (normally), but partial-state question if router receive() absorbs revert.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: LP/redeemer loses dcntEth and receives no ETH if partial state commits.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Wrong lifecycle ordering with external call; NEEDS_HARNESS for partial-execution scenario.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: wrong lifecycle ordering / external-call failure in redeemEth and removeLiquidityEth — dcntEth burned/transferred before ETH delivery
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: sequential ops with no rollback guard beyond Solidity atomic revert.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether complete revert atomicity holds under all failure modes or partial state can persist (router receive() fallback).
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Redeemer/LP loses dcntEth with no ETH if partial state commits.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: access-control mismatch on redeemEth/redeemWeth (unauthorized callers redeem dcntEth)
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: Caller must hold dcntEth and call transferFrom — the ERC20 transferFrom is the authorization gate; dcntEth represents bridge credit redeemable for ETH/WETH.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Without dcntEth balance the transferFrom reverts; no caller extracts WETH without equal-value dcntEth (absent the double-withdrawal bug already captured).

impact_direction.attacker_receives: X ETH profit (double withdrawal: redeemEth + removeLiquidityEth using unchanged balanceOf credit).
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Initial deposit position (balanceOf not cleared after redeemEth).
impact_direction.victim_loses: Other LPs lose proportional share of WETH reserves; reserve drained 2X for X deposited.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: balanceOf[LP] must equal outstanding liquidity claim — violated because redeemEth/redeemWeth don't decrement balanceOf; WETH-reserve==dcntEth-supply invariant broken.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Permissionless after deposit; scales with deposit size; not admin-gated; not timing-dependent.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: off-by-one reserves-check (Medium) + wrong-lifecycle external-call (NEEDS_HARNESS) carried with distinct victims/state
